pr_title: subsys: l2: Properly terminate LCP state at modem side when closing down
pr_body:
Takes the modem state machine by calling lcp_close instead of lcp_down
Using this method the LCP layer sends a TERMINATE_REQ to the modem and the
network interface is only taken down when the LCP layer has properly finished.
Moved the ppp_mgmt_raise_carrier_off_event and net_if_carrier_down
to lcp.c to avoid breaking the interface.
Tested on a real modem.

Fixes: zephyrproject-rtos#41627

Signed-off-by: Sjors Hettinga <s.a.hettinga@gmail.com>
pr_comments:
@jukkar Thanks for your quick feedback on style, Is there a way to run the style check offline, apart from the CI toolchain?
Could you also check the change for contents and way of implementing?

> Could you also check the change for contents and way of implementing?

The change looks okeyish, unfortunately I have no way to test it atm. Lets see what other reviewers have to say.

The previous path took the LCP state machine down, without sending an actual terminate to the modem. This left the LCP state machine in the opened state at the modem side. In my case (without gsm_mux) this prevented it from answering to AT commands after closing down the connection. This is how I verified functionality.
In the new situation, the lcp_close function is called instead of the lcp_down, which sends out a TERMINATE_REQ to the modem, which it has to respond to with an TERMINATE_ACK. As the code shown here is called from a workqueue, we cannot wait for the TERMINATE_ACK to arrive and the final closing statements have been moved to the used callback function lcp_finished.
In this new situation the statements ppp_mgmt_raise_carrier_off_event(ctx->iface); and net_if_carrier_down(ctx->iface); are just delayed until the LCP connection has properly been terminated. Calling net_if_carrier_down earlier would prevent sending out LCP messages and properly terminating.
A new rebase of main, to so some unrelated build issues

issue_context.title: PPP_L2 does not properly terminate the modem state machine when going down.
issue_context.body:
In ppp_l2, when an ppp connection is started by ppp_enable(ctx,true), it calls ppp_lcp->open, in the function start_ppp. There is no such stop_ppp function that calls ppp_lcp->close when ppp_enable(ctx,false)

Unless the modem itself closes the the connection, the LCP layer will not properly terminate and the modem stays in the data mode instead of in command mode. A proper ppp_lcp->close sequence in combination with ppp_lcp->down could fix this.

In the current situation there is a mismatch between the LCP state machine and modem state machine after a connection down.

To reproduce:
Use the GSM_PPP and see the modem not responding to AT commands after shutting down the PPP connection.

I'll try to create proper fix.
comments:
Looked at the issue today. I can set call an ppp_lcp->close instead of ppp_lcp->down in ppp_enable(ctx, false),  but have to wait for the connection to properly shutdown, before shutting down the carrier. Otherwise all LCP transmission is blocked by the net_if layer. The LCP layer has callbacks for this purpose, but they do not propagate to the up to the ppp_l2 file. 

The carrier off statement can be moved to the lcp_finished function in the lcp.c, but a more neat solution would be to propagate the lcp_down and lcp_finished callbacks to the ppp_l2 layer. Although this requires an interface change.

Do you want me to send a pull request in for the initial fix, without interface break?

review_comments:
Minor nit about the commit subject, no need to mention literal `subsys` there,
just do `net: ppp: Properly .....`

Thanks for looking into it. The challenge is that I have a different implementation of the layers on higher level (proprietary legacy). This makes it slightly different in behavior.

The problem you are dealing with it that you shutdown the modem too early. So it did not have time to finish the sequence. This means that your GSM MUX is not switched properly back to AT mode and it will never respond to AT mode.
In my shutdown sequence I call the ppps_close function, then wait for a semaphore. This semaphore is being raised when the NET_EVENT_IF_DOWN event comes from the net_mgmt_event_callback. This is only triggered by the net_if_carrier_down(ctx->iface); being called in the lcp_finished function. This way you allow the state machine to properly finish the terminate sequence before cutting the power. This will even be reached when the number of retries is exhausted.

With respect to your last suggestion. This will cancel the effect of the new changes will be cancelled. The ppp_lcp->close will put the packet in the TX queue, but by the time the queue is being severed after this function, the interface has been shut down, so no packet will be send and you will probably bump into the line: NET_WARN("iface %p is down", iface); in net_if.c

It obviously needs some more work to work with the stock example. Due to COVID I have no access to HW and debugger today. If you could point me to an example from the examples folder I can try to make it work on my HW.

> The ->enable(iface, false) triggers the close, but the gsm->mux_enabled = false; needs to be delayed for the FSM to finish its termination.

Indeed, good catch. @ssharks would you be able to send a fix for this?

I can give it a try. It will be earliest next week as I need some HW to test this. Next the GSM_PPP driver is quite device specific at the moment, so I need to adjust it to the device I have as well.

Do you want to have it in a separate commit, i.e. separate pull request or how to send in these separate but somewhat related changes.
I think separate PR would be better here.
